cta.title: Ship every language with every release.

byok.body: Anthropic, OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including local models. Costs are shown per job and capped by a budget.
byok.title: Bring your own key

glossary.body: glossary.toml lives next to your code. Required translations, forbidden terms and do-not-translate words are enforced, not suggested.
glossary.title: Glossary as code

lockfile.body: glot.lock hashes every source and target. Only the delta gets translated, and hand edits are never overwritten.
lockfile.title: Lockfile

mcp.body: Claude Code, Cursor and friends query keys, glossary and issues directly, and translate with file:line references and UI role.

oss.body: MIT licensed. CLI, MCP server, API and this dashboard. Self-host it, fork it, audit it.

features.subtitle: The LLM is always surrounded by deterministic code.
features.title: Built for teams that ship with agents

validator.body: ICU, i18next and MessageFormat 2 parsing. Placeholders, tags and plural categories checked for every locale. Failures are retried, then escalated to a stronger model.
validator.title: Deterministic validator

visual.body: Playwright renders every locale and flags overflow, truncation and RTL layout breaks before your users see them.
visual.title: Visual QA

fit.afterAlt: Shorter German label that fits the button
fit.beforeAlt: German button label cut off with an ellipsis
fit.body: German is often a third longer than English. glot fit captures your running app in every locale, measures each text against its container, asks the LLM for a shorter variant that keeps the meaning and the placeholders, then renders again.
fit.caption: Real captures from the demo app, German locale.
fit.p1: Measured in the browser, not guessed from a character count
fit.p2: Shortened variants still pass the validator and glossary
fit.p3: Stops after a fixed number of passes, never loops on cost
fit.title: Translations that fit the button

hero.badge: Open source · MIT · Bring your own LLM key
hero.subtitle: Point glot at a codebase full of hardcoded strings. One command moves them to keys and rewrites your components; your LLM translates, deterministic code checks every string, and the result lands in Git.
hero.terminal: From hardcoded English to four languages
hero.title: i18n your AI agent can't break.

insights.body: An anonymous beacon counts visitors by preferred language and the locale you served them, then compares conversion. No cookie, no visitor id.
insights.title: Insights per language

install.subtitle: Run it locally with your agent, or connect it to a glot server for your team.

more.subtitle: Quality you can check without speaking the language, and data on which language to add next.

ondevice.body: For languages you don't ship yet, @glot/runtime translates in the browser with the built-in Translator API, then runs glot's validator compiled to WebAssembly.

overlay.alt: glot overlay popover showing a key, its source and its translations in five languages
overlay.body: The dev overlay finds the key behind the text you clicked, shows it in every locale with live validator issues, and saves to your catalog files. Hot reload does the rest.
overlay.p1: AI actions: suggest, shorten, more formal, translate all
overlay.p2: Flags text that overflows its container
overlay.p3: Dev only, about 6 kB gzipped, no runtime dependencies
overlay.title: Alt+click any text in your app

experiments.title: Experiments
experiments.subtitle: The translation that converts best, per locale. glot writes validated variants of a high-stakes string and lets your visitors pick the winner.
experiments.meta: goal {goal} · {pct}% of traffic · min {n} per arm
experiments.sourceChanged: The source text changed since these variants were written: they are no longer served. Stop this experiment and start a new one.
experiments.noTraffic: No visitor yet. Variants are served by @glot/insights to visitors of this locale.
experiments.promoteBody: “{value}” becomes the official {locale} translation of {key} (reviewed, in the key history). It ships with your next glot pull, CDN refresh or PR, like any edit. The other variants stop.
experiments.keepBody: The official translation converted best. The experiment closes and nothing changes in your catalogs.
experiments.promotedToast: Done: the catalog now holds the winning wording
experiments.stoppedToast: Experiment stopped: everyone sees the official translation
experiments.chartCaption: Each curve is the plausible range of an arm's conversion rate given the data so far; narrower means more certain.

explain.burnIn: Every arm gets equal traffic until it reaches the minimum sample; then traffic shifts toward the arms that convert.
explain.running: Traffic follows the evidence (Thompson sampling). A winner is declared when one arm is best with more than 95 % probability, checked each time traffic doubles.
explain.decided: {name} is best with {p} probability. Losers are no longer served; promote it to make it official.
explain.officialWins: The official translation converts best. Variants are no longer served.
explain.promoted: The winning wording is now the official translation.
explain.stopped: Stopped: everyone sees the official translation.

empty.title: Find the wording that converts
empty.body: Pick a CTA or a pricing headline and a locale. glot writes 2-3 variants with the same meaning in different tones, validates them, serves them to a share of your visitors and tells you which one wins.

dialog.title: New copy experiment
dialog.body: Variants keep the meaning, placeholders and glossary of the official translation; only those that pass validation are ever served.
dialog.keyHint: A high-stakes string: call to action, pricing title, signup button.
dialog.guardrails: The official translation stays in the race as the reference. Traffic % is the share of visitors exposed to the experiment; the rest always see the official text.
dialog.created: {n, plural, one {# variant} other {# variants}} validated and live{rejected, plural, =0 {} other {, # rejected}}
